title: Broken ground truth and missing data-table evaluation in Berk-Hath Investment Package and DCF sensitivity tables
evidence:
The sole verifier `SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check` (`verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells`, weight: 1.0) grades 210 modification cells across 4 sheets against `gt_02_golden.xlsx`, requiring `mod_ratio == 1.0` to pass (`spreadsheetbench2.py:372`). Two compounding defects make 100 of the 210 modification cells (47.6% of modified cells, controlling 100% of the binary score) impossible or mathematically invalid to pass:

1. **Verifier strips data-table formulas before recalculation**: The input workbook contains 100 what-if data-table cells (`=TABLE(...)` in `DCF!V10:Z14` and `Berk-Hath Investment Package!G10:K14, G18:K22, G26:K30`). `verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells` runs `managed_recalculated_xlsx(Path(output_path), force_recalculation=True)` (`spreadsheetbench2.py:364`), which calls `freeze_datatable_formulas` (`libreoffice.py:390`) to strip `<f>` tags from all `TABLE(...)` cells and then runs LibreOffice with `OOXMLRecalcMode=0` (forced recalculation) without invoking `with_computed_tables` (`data_tables.py:99`). Any submission that preserves the workbook's `TABLE(...)` formulas—or edits the workbook with `openpyxl` as instructed in `problem.py`—has its data-table cells stripped or left with stale/empty `<v>` cache values during grading.

2. **Invalid golden values in `Berk-Hath Investment Package!G11:K14` (20 cells)**: In `Berk-Hath Investment Package`, the first sensitivity table (`G10:K14`) varies Annual Dividend Rate (`C12`, fixed from `8` to `0.08`) down the column header `F10:F14` (`0.07`, `0.075`, `0.08`, `0.085`, `0.09`), where `F10 = F11 - $F$7`, `F11 = F12 - $F$7`, `F12 = C12`, `F13 = F12 + $F$7`, `F14 = F13 + $F$7`. Because the column headers `F10:F14` are formulas that depend on the data-table input cell `C12` itself, substituting `F11` (`0.075`) into `C12` during Excel's sequential data-table evaluation shifts `F12` to `0.075`, `F13` to `0.08`, and `F14` to `0.085` mid-table. Consequently, `gt_02_golden.xlsx` stores corrupted values: Row 11 (`7.5%`) and Row 12 (`8.0%`) have identical values (`G11 = G12 = 11152.8830`, `H11 = H12 = 10782.6394`, `I11 = I12 = 10429.3142`, `J11 = J12 = 10092.0287`, `K11 = K12 = 9769.9543`), Row 13 (`8.5%`) duplicates Row 10 (`7.0%`, e.g., `G13 = G10 = 11515.7129`), and Row 14 (`9.0%`) holds the true `8.0%` base-case values (`I14 = 11468.3953` instead of `I12`). True financial values for `7.5%`, `8.0%`, `8.5%`, and `9.0%` dividend rates (e.g., `G11 = 11878.5427`, `G12 = 12241.3726`, `G13 = 12604.2024`, `G14 = 12967.0323`, as computed in Unit 2) are marked wrong by the verifier (`Modification error at Berk-Hath Investment Package!G11: answer=11152.8830174067, output=11878.5427134403`).
confirmation: Confirmed the GT's first Berk-Hath data table is corrupted by headers F10:F14 that depend on input cell C12 (F12 =C12): I11=I12=10429.31 and I14=11468.40 (the true 8% value), so 20 of the 210 modification cells hold invalid answers.
fix: Same GT fix to G11:K14. The other half of this finding (the verifier freezes TABLE() cells instead of evaluating them) is harness behaviour and is not changed here.

title: Golden sensitivity table contains twenty incorrect required answers
evidence: In the golden workbook, 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G11:K14 does not reconcile with the table's dividend-rate and discount-rate headers or the package valuation formulas. For example, G12 uses an 8% dividend rate, 6.3% discount rate, 10-year term, 10,000 face value, 10,500 redemption value and 736.333882 warrant value. These produce 12,241.372561, but the golden answer is 11,152.883017. G11 and G12 incorrectly contain identical values despite different dividend rates. Recomputing the table identifies twenty discrepancies exceeding the verifier's 1% tolerance. These are modification cells, all of which must match for the sole verifier, weighted 1, to award any credit; a correctly rebuilt sensitivity table therefore fails.
confirmation: GT G12 (8% dividend, 6.3% discount, 10-year term) is 11152.88, identical to G11, while the GT's own second table gives 12241.37 for the same inputs (G20), so the 20 cells G11:K14 are wrong answer-key values.

title: The answer key has wrong values in the Berk-Hath dividend-rate × discount-rate sensitivity table (G11:K14)
evidence: Every cell in the graded ranges counts, and all modification cells must match the answer key for the only verifier (weight 1) to pass. In gt_02_golden.xlsx, the first Berk-Hath data table (TABLE($F$9,$C$12,F10:F14,$C$15,G9:K9)) holds hardcoded values that do not follow the model. I recomputed it from the GT inputs (face value 10,000, quarterly convention ignored as in C19, PV of the annual dividend over 10 years, plus 10,500 redemption, plus the 736.33 warrant). Expected values at a 0.073 discount rate: dividend 0.07 → 10,775.67, 0.075 → 11,122.03, 0.08 → 11,468.40, 0.085 → 11,814.76, 0.09 → 12,161.12. GT I10:I14 = 10,775.67, 10,429.31, 10,429.31, 10,775.67, 11,468.40. Rows 11 and 12 are identical, row 13 repeats row 10, and the values do not rise with the dividend rate. The GT also contradicts itself: I12 (div 8%, disc 7.3%, term 10) = 10,429.31, but the second table's I20 (same inputs) = 11,468.40. Only row 10 is correct. Rows 11–14 (20 graded cells) are wrong.
confirmation: GT I10:I14 = 10775.67, 10429.31, 10429.31, 10775.67, 11468.40, which do not rise with the dividend rate, and I12 (8%, 7.3%, 10 yrs) conflicts with I20 = 11468.40 for the same inputs in the second table, so G11:K14 are wrong.

title: SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check: Verifier fails to evaluate data tables and compares Berk-Hath Investment Package!G11:K14 against corrupted ground-truth values
evidence: `SpreadsheetBench 2 official cell check` (`verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells`, weight: 1.0) scored 0.0 across all 3 units (unit 1: mod=0.5810, unit 2: mod=0.9048, unit 3: mod=0.5810). In Unit 2 (steps `[52]`–`[60]`) and Unit 3 (steps `[58]`–`[65]`), the agent identified that LibreOffice does not evaluate Excel `=TABLE(...)` formulas properly and explicitly computed the mathematically exact sensitivity table values in Python, writing them into `output.xlsx` (`DCF!V10:Z14` and `Berk-Hath Investment Package!G10:K14, G18:K22, G26:K30`). In Unit 2, the agent also fixed all 4 ground-truth modifications (`DCF!I20:R20`, `Synergies!D35=0.25`, `Berk-Hath Investment Package!C12=0.08`, and `F38` cleared). However, `verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells` flagged 20 modification errors in `Berk-Hath Investment Package!G11:K14` (e.g., `Modification error at Berk-Hath Investment Package!G11: answer=11152.8830174067, output=11878.5427134403`). As confirmed by inspecting `gt_02_golden.xlsx`, the golden workbook's `G11:K14` values are corrupted by a circular header dependency in `F10:F14` (`F12 = C12`, where `C12` is the data-table column input cell), causing `gt_02_golden.xlsx` to have duplicate values in rows 11 and 12 (`G11 = G12 = 11152.8830`, which is actually the 7.0% dividend rate value at `6.8%` or `6.3%` step shift) and placing the base-case 8.0% dividend value (`11468.3953` at 7.3% discount rate) in row 14 (`I14`, labeled 9.0% dividend rate) instead of row 12 (`I12`, labeled 8.0% dividend rate). Furthermore, if an agent leaves the `=TABLE(...)` formulas intact and updates cached `<v>` tags (as Unit 3 did in steps `[63]`–`[65]`), `verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells` calls `managed_recalculated_xlsx(..., force_recalculation=True)` (`spreadsheetbench2.py:364`), which strips `<f>` tags only for `TABLE(...)` cells while force-recalculating all other cells—and if an agent uses `openpyxl` (which does not write `<v>` tags), `freeze_datatable_formulas` leaves all 100 data-table cells as `None`. Additionally, `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages` is `0700 root:root`, causing `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openpyxl'` in step `[1]`/`[2]` of every unit despite `problem.py` stating `Pandas`, `openpyxl`, and `numpy` are available.
confirmation: gt_02_golden.xlsx Berk-Hath G11:K14 are wrong: G11=G12=11152.88 and row 13 repeats row 10, while the 8%/6.3%/10-year case equals 12241.37 in the GT's own second table (G20); these 20 graded modification cells make a correct solution fail the all-or-nothing check.
fix: gt_02_golden.xlsx, 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G11:K14 (20 hardcoded data-table results): replaced the corrupted values with the table's own model, PV(disc,10,-div*10000)+PV(disc,10,0,-10500)+736.33388 warrant, at dividend rates 7.5%/8%/8.5%/9% (F11:F14) and discount rates 6.3%-8.3% (G9:K9). Examples: G11 11152.88 -> 11878.54, I12 10429.31 -> 11468.40 (now equals the second table's I20), K14 10762.99 -> 11425.01. Row 10, which was already right, reproduces exactly under the same formula. No other cell changed. The patched GT scores 1.0 on the local SB2 cell check.
